extracted.intended_audience: young physician-scientists (assistant professors) and institutional nominating officials applying for the Damon Runyon Clinical Investigator Award
extracted.subtask_short: Damon Runyon Clinical Investigator Award application
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and selection standards for applicants and institutions seeking the Damon Runyon Clinical Investigator Award — a 3‑year career-development grant for early independent physician‑scientists doing disease‑oriented cancer research. Covers eligibility, selection criteria, funding rules, award terms, loan repayment, and application procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence of the applicant and Mentor
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection gives priority to the overall excellence of both the applicant and the Mentor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CIAC explicitly lists 'Excellence of the applicant and Mentor' as a selection criterion. Mentor excellence implies capacity to train and advocate for the applicant. Evidence may include track record, publications, mentoring history, and institutional support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation, creativity, quality and originality of the research proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals are evaluated on their innovation, creativity, scientific quality, and originality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CIAC 'puts a premium on innovation and creativity' when reviewing applications. Reviewers assess whether the research uses novel concepts or approaches and whether it is high-quality and original.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentor and institution commitment to development and training
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrated commitment of the Mentor and institution to develop the applicant into an independent clinical, translational, or outcomes-based investigator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers consider letters and institutional support materials showing protected time, start-up package, space, mentoring plan, and tangible institutional commitment to career development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence of applicant’s commitment and translational ability
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence that the applicant is committed to clinical translational and/or cancer prevention research and can apply laboratory advances to clinical problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should show prior and planned translational activity, patient-oriented focus, and an ability to bridge lab and clinic; specifics in the research plan and past work strengthen this criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance of the proposed research to cancer and/or cancer prevention
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of how important and potentially impactful the proposed project is to the field of cancer research or cancer prevention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Importance includes potential to advance practice of cancer medicine, address unmet needs, or lead to meaningful clinical advances. Reviewers will weigh significance alongside innovation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to the Foundation’s definition of clinical research
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposal must align with the Foundation's defined categories of clinical research: (a) patient-oriented research, (b) epidemiologic and behavioral studies, and (c) outcomes and health services research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patient-oriented research explicitly includes human subjects or human-derived materials, diagnostic/therapeutic interventions, clinical trials, and new technologies for detection/treatment/prevention. Proposals outside these categories may be judged ineligible or less competitive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to the 'Handshake Rule' (patient‑involved clinical research)
rubrics_metrics.description: Preference is given to projects where the physician conducts research studies that directly involve patients (the 'Handshake Rule'); this rule does not apply to pathologist candidates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects that directly involve patient interaction will be favored. Pathologists are exempt from this preference. Applicants should state clearly if their research directly involves patients and how.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protected research effort — minimum 80% commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must commit a minimum of 80% of their full-time professional effort to research during each award year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Waiver of the 80% requirement may be considered only in very rare, unique circumstances, with a compelling written justification by the Department Chair specifying guaranteed percentage of effort and safeguards to protect research time. Reviewers will expect clear institutional support for protected time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentor workload and application limits
rubrics_metrics.description: No more than two Damon Runyon Clinical Investigators (including Co-Mentors) may be funded to work with the same Mentor at any given time; only one application will be accepted from a Mentor per review session (including Co‑Mentors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This limits Mentor capacity. Mentors should disclose existing Damon Runyon advisees; institutions should ensure compliance. Multiple applications listing the same Mentor in one review session are not permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional nomination and invited-institution requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each applicant must be nominated by their institution, and applications are only accepted from institutions invited by the Foundation. Three nominations per invited institution (including affiliated schools) are allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions must be on the Foundation's invited list; institutional officials control nominations and must adhere to the three‑nomination cap. Applicants should coordinate with institutional nominating authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faculty rank and timing eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must hold an independent Assistant Professor position or equivalent at a U.S. institution and must apply within the first four years of that appointment (cut‑off date noted on page). Instructor, adjunct, and acting positions are not eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page lists a specific cut-off date (e.g., July 1, 2022 for the current cycle). Applicants must verify their appointment dates and status meet this window; only up to two application attempts are permitted in the eligibility period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree, training, board eligibility, and license requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must have an MD, DO, or MD/PhD, have completed subspecialty training, be U.S. Board eligible, and hold a valid active U.S. medical license at time of application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are strict eligibility conditions; applicants lacking required degrees/training or an active license are ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on holding R01/R01‑equivalent awards at application
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates holding or awarded R01s (or R01-equivalent grants such as the DP2 and DP5) at the time of application are not eligible to apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must disclose current funding; having major independent NIH-equivalent awards disqualifies the candidate for this program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent funding restrictions (private mentored awards)
rubrics_metrics.description: No other physician‑scientist mentored career development award from a private source (non‑federal government) may be held concurrently with this Award; federal K‑type awards are allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed concurrent federal awards include NIH K08, K12, K23, DoD, and VA career development awards. If holding other awards, applicants must clarify relationships and ensure no prohibited concurrent private mentored awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific or budgetary overlap prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific or budgetary overlap with other funded projects is not allowed; all current and pending support must be reported and relationships explained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should clearly describe how the Damon Runyon‑funded project is distinct from other support and avoid duplicative aims or budget items. Failure to disclose or explain overlap can render an application noncompliant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of funds and indirect cost prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Funds ($600,000 total; $200,000 per year) are flexible for scientific needs (investigator stipend/fringe up to $130,000 annually, personnel, equipment, supplies), but no part of the grant can be used for indirect costs/institutional overhead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget submissions must allocate funds to permissible categories and not include indirect costs. Applicants should plan budgets accordingly and justify major items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Loan repayment program eligibility and documentation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: To qualify for Damon Runyon loan repayment (up to $100,000 aggregated during award), candidates must first apply to the NIH Loan Repayment Program and submit documentation for qualifying loans within one month of acceptance and annually thereafter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Qualifying loans are for tuition and direct educational expenses from government, academic, or commercial lenders; consolidated loans are partially eligible per ratio of qualifying vs non‑qualifying components. Participants must disclose other repayment agreements and provide receipts, loan agreements, and payment information annually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Loan repayment payment rules, limits, and payback conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Damon Runyon will pay qualifying loan payments up to $33,333 per year (aggregate up to $100,000 over three years); participants must refund amounts if they terminate the Award early unless Foundation waives payback for continued clinical investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If annual qualifying payments exceed $33,333, the Foundation will determine which loans to pay. Repayments stop during leaves of absence unless written permission granted. Delinquent/defaulted loans, loans from individuals, late fees, or non-qualifying expenses are excluded from repayment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tax reimbursement policy for loan repayments
rubrics_metrics.description: Loan repayments are taxable to participants; the Foundation will approximate and pay an 'Additional Tax Payment' to offset increased tax liabilities, using the Foundation‑determined assumed tax rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The assumed tax rate is at the Foundation's discretion and may not equal the actual participant tax rate. These Additional Tax Payments may be reclaimed if participant terminates early as part of the payback agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publications and presentations acknowledgement requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All publications (including abstracts) resulting from Damon Runyon‑supported projects must include a specific acknowledgment: '[Name of Awardee] is a Damon Runyon Clinical Investigator supported (in part) by the Damon Runyon Cancer Research Foundation (CI-#[___]).' Awardees should identify themselves as Damon Runyon Clinical Investigators when presenting work and may use the provided Foundation logo in materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistent acknowledgment helps Foundation visibility and compliance. Awardees should download and use the official logo for presentations/posters as instructed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award administration, terms, and invention policy adherence
rubrics_metrics.description: All awardees must adhere to the Foundation's Award Statement and Invention Policy; awards are made to the sponsoring institution (not creating an employer‑employee relationship with the Foundation), and policies will not be modified at institutions' requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions and awardees must accept Foundation policies as written. Intellectual property disclosure and invention policy forms are required; Foundation retains discretion on policy enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfers, termination, and prior approval requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If an Awardee wishes to discontinue the project, leave the institution, or modify award agreements, they must obtain prior approval from the Foundation; failure to do so results in immediate termination and may jeopardize future institutional awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awardees must notify and secure Foundation approval before major changes. Unauthorized transfers/changes lead to termination and possible institutional consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attendance and community engagement expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: All current Clinical Investigators are expected to attend the annual Accelerating Cancer Cures Symposium to highlight achievements and interact with sponsors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attendance is an expectation of award participation; applicants/awardees should plan to attend and engage in Foundation activities and sponsor interactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuation Grant purpose and eligibility context
rubrics_metrics.description: A Continuation Grant can provide two additional years of support for Clinical Investigators approaching the end of their award who need extra time/funding to complete promising research or to initiate/continue a clinical trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuation is intended for well‑justified needs near award end; applicants should follow forms and processes for continuation applications and demonstrate progress and reason for extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application procedures and deadline compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must be submitted via Altum | Proposal Central and follow the Damon Runyon Application Guidelines; a specific deadline/time is enforced (e.g., Jan 20, 2026, 4:00 pm ET).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must use the proper portal, complete required forms in Proposal Central, and meet the stated deadline. Late or improper submissions risk ineligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity, equity, inclusion, and reviewer bias awareness statement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation states an uncompromising commitment to excellence and values diversity, equity, and inclusion; reviewers are instructed to be aware of potential unconscious biases during review, scoring, and discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review sessions begin with a read statement to acknowledge unconscious bias. This is guidance for reviewers to mitigate bias and for applicants to know the Foundation's DEI emphasis.
